concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.summary: Describe how an algorithm's running time grows with input size, ignoring constants.

concepts.name: Recursion
concepts.summary: Solve a problem by calling the same method on a smaller input until a base case.

concepts.name: ArrayLists
concepts.summary: A resizable array that doubles capacity when full, giving amortized O(1) adds at the back.

concepts.name: Amortized analysis
concepts.summary: Average the cost of an operation over a sequence so rare expensive steps are spread out.

concepts.name: Linked lists
concepts.summary: Nodes holding data and next (and previous) pointers, with O(1) adds at the head.

concepts.name: Stacks and queues
concepts.summary: LIFO and FIFO collections built on arrays or linked lists.

concepts.name: Iterators
concepts.summary: Objects that step through a collection one element at a time through hasNext and next.

concepts.name: Tree traversals
concepts.summary: Visit every node of a binary tree in preorder, inorder, postorder, or level-order.

concepts.name: Binary search trees
concepts.summary: A binary tree where left < node < right, supporting search, add and remove in O(log n) on average.
concepts.source: Binary search trees: search, add, remove

concepts.name: Heaps and priority queues
concepts.summary: A complete binary tree where each parent is smaller than its children, used as a priority queue.

concepts.name: AVL trees
concepts.summary: A self-balancing BST that uses rotations to keep heights within one.

concepts.name: HashMaps
concepts.summary: Store key-value pairs in an array indexed by a hash of the key, with a strategy for collisions.

concepts.name: Simple sorts
concepts.summary: Bubble, insertion and selection sort, each O(n^2) in the worst case.

concepts.name: Merge sort and quick sort
concepts.summary: Sort by splitting the input, sorting the parts recursively, and combining them in O(n log n).

concepts.name: Pattern matching
concepts.summary: Find a pattern in text faster than brute force using Boyer-Moore or KMP tables.

concepts.name: BFS and DFS
concepts.summary: Explore a graph level by level with a queue or deeply with a stack or recursion.

concepts.name: Dijkstra's algorithm
concepts.summary: Find shortest paths from one vertex using a priority queue of tentative distances.

concepts.name: Minimum spanning trees
concepts.summary: Connect all vertices with the least total edge weight using Prim's or Kruskal's algorithm.

edges.reason: amortized cost is a Big-O bound
BFS uses a queue, DFS a stack
